method: Machine-learned crop suitability (model crop-suitability-v3.1): one XGBoost model per crop, trained on where 40 crops are grown today (IFPRI MapSPAM 2020, 22,450 farmland cells worldwide), each cell described by 10 climate features from six NASA POWER measurements, 2001 to 2025. On regions held out of training it tells places that grow a crop from places that do not with AUC 0.90. Rain only also needs enough rain: scores fade to 0 below 100 mm a year (200 mm is full strength for wheat and barley, 250 mm for other crops). Future years: each feature's own 2001 to 2025 trend (Theil-Sen) continued, with a 95% range from 200 resamples of the years. Not a forecast.
source: NASA POWER climate and a model trained on IFPRI MapSPAM 2020 crop maps
score_note: A score runs from 0 to 100: how typical this climate is of the places where the crop is grown today. 50 means as typical of places that grow it as of places that do not. It is not a yield and not the chance of a good harvest. Irrigated assumes water can be supplied; it does not show that water exists here. Rain only uses the NASA POWER rain record, which jumps around 2015 over Egypt, so read rain only changes with care. Crops Egypt grows only on small areas (soybean, sunflower, chickpea, lentil) can score low even where they are grown. Olive and date palm are not separate crops in the crop maps and are not covered.
